title: Working With Strings and Numbers
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of working with strings and numbers in a jQuery application.
Apply string trimming with native methods in a small example and describe its expected result.
Verify number parsing with an explicit test or browser observation.
status_note: Draft generated from the attached syllabus and official references; requires lesson-by-lesson technical review, local execution, accessibility checks, and editorial approval.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will work through working with strings and numbers with a focused jQuery example. The subtopics below preserve the supplied curriculum coverage and connect the API idea to a small browser interface.
content.why_it_matters: This topic is useful because it turns string trimming with native methods into a repeatable implementation choice. Static jQuery utilities help process values and collections, but current JavaScript already provides Array, Object, Map, Set, and String APIs. Prefer the clearest supported API.

The test setup and any runtime limitation are documented honestly.

common_mistakes: Assuming a selector matched an element without checking the collection length.
Confusing jQuery collections with native DOM elements or live properties with markup attributes.
Using .html() with untrusted data or assuming client-side validation enforces server rules.
Treating a demo snippet as production-ready without testing failure and accessibility states.
